blocks.content: kubectl delete removes objects, by name, by label selector, or by pointing at the exact manifest that created them, and it follows the same graceful shutdown sequence covered throughout this course.
The simplest form removes exactly one, specifically named object, precise and unambiguous.

blocks.alt: One specific object, removed by its exact name

blocks.content: Using the exact selector mechanism covered in the Pods module, delete can remove every object matching a given label at once, useful for cleaning up a whole related group without listing each name individually.

blocks.alt: Every matching object removed at once, using the same selector mechanism from the Pods module

blocks.content: delete -f removes exactly whatever a given manifest file defines, a clean, symmetrical counterpart to apply -f, tearing down precisely what was previously created.

blocks.alt: The clean, symmetrical counterpart to apply -f, removing exactly what was declared

blocks.content: 4. It Is Still a Graceful Deletion
blocks.text: 4. It Is Still a Graceful Deletion

blocks.content: This connects directly to the Pod Lifecycle topic, deleting a Pod does not kill it instantly, it triggers the same SIGTERM, grace period, then SIGKILL sequence covered there, giving the application a real chance to shut down cleanly.

blocks.alt: The exact same graceful shutdown sequence covered in the Pod Lifecycle topic

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: kubectl delete removes objects by name, by label selector (matching many at once), or by pointing at the exact manifest that created them.
Deletion is graceful by default, following the same SIGTERM-then-grace-period-then-SIGKILL sequence covered in the Pod Lifecycle topic.
